rules_and_verification.enforced_by: storage_lock_safety.py contains zero VACUUM execute() calls anywhere; delete_bounded_batch() explicitly rejects VACUUM in where_clause
no ALTER/CREATE TABLE/DROP TABLE statement anywhere in storage_lock_safety.py
delete_bounded_batch() commits after each bounded batch, never holds BEGIN EXCLUSIVE
LockSafetyBudget.max_transaction_seconds tracked via time.monotonic() around each batch
PRAGMA busy_timeout set before every write attempt in delete_bounded_batch()
DatabaseBusyError raised on lock contention beyond busy_timeout, caller expected to skip -- no retry loop exists in this module
acquire_cleanup_lease() uses fcntl.flock(LOCK_EX | LOCK_NB), second concurrent caller raises CleanupLeaseHeldError immediately (non-blocking)
cleanup never uses BEGIN EXCLUSIVE or blocking retry; a real writer's IMMEDIATE/EXCLUSIVE transaction always wins within busy_timeout
storage_monitor.py measure_db() reads the -wal sidecar file size as part of every snapshot
rules_and_verification.test: live measurement this session: flex_complete_database.db WAL=17.7MB, wt_ops_v2.db WAL=19.9MB

rules_and_verification.enforced_by: delete_bounded_batch() calls conn.rollback() on any sqlite3.OperationalError before re-raising; verify_db_valid_after_cleanup() runs PRAGMA integrity_check

each batch is an independent transaction; an interrupted run leaves committed batches committed and uncommitted work rolled back, so a subsequent run continues from wherever the WHERE clause naturally resumes
eligible_for_pressure_state() checks NO_AUTOMATED_DELETION_CLASSES BEFORE consulting the pressure-state allow-list, so no pressure-state misconfiguration can make a PERMANENT class eligible

rules_and_verification.rule: stale lease does not permanently block cleanup
rules_and_verification.enforced_by: flock is tied to the holding process's file descriptor, released automatically on process exit regardless of file content

rules_and_verification.rule: no duplicate deletion / no partial segment retirement
rules_and_verification.enforced_by: retire_closed_segment() checks os.path.exists(dest) BEFORE os.rename(), raising FileExistsError rather than overwriting; source file is left completely untouched on failure

test_execution.fixtures_used: isolated tmp_path SQLite databases only -- zero references to any real database/ path (verified by test_all_db_paths_used_in_tests_are_tmp_path_fixtures)

watchtower_preservation_during_testing: All fixture databases are created fresh in pytest tmp_path directories per test; the real database/wt_ops_v2.db and database/flex_complete_database.db were never opened for write by any test in this suite.
preferred_mechanism_confirmed: Whole closed-segment retirement (os.rename, atomic on same filesystem) avoids SQLite row-level locking entirely -- confirmed as the preferred mechanism per Part 13, and it is the ONLY mutation primitive in this module that requires zero SQLite lock at all (delete_bounded_batch necessarily does acquire a write lock, bounded and safe, but retire_closed_segment does not touch SQLite locking machinery at all).
